headline: One Death, Six Proposals, Thin Data: Malaysia's Drunk Driving Blind Spot
context: A driver positive for alcohol and drugs killed Lalamove rider Amirul Hafiz Omar, 33, in Klang on 29 March 2026. Politicians demanded the death penalty. The current penalty is already 10-15 years. Only 149 DUI crash cases were charged from 2021 to September 2024.

changes.summary: Correction: Replaced an unverified claim that alcohol is found in 25% to 30% of Australian fatal crashes with the fact that Australia blood-tests every driver in a fatal crash.

Correction: we said 149 drink-driving crash cases were charged in three years and 1,261 convictions came in one year, but the periods were nearly four years and 11 months; the 12 alcohol cases count fatal crashes, not deaths, a New South Wales police power replaces a claim about all of Australia, and an unsourced claim about breath-test data is removed.

cards.big: A drunk, drugged driver killed a father of three. Politicians demanded the death penalty. The penalty is already 10-15 years.
cards.sub: On 29 March 2026 in Klang, a driver positive for alcohol and drugs struck motorcyclist Amirul Hafiz Omar, 33, head-on. He worked two jobs to support three children.

cards.big: 149 DUI crash cases charged from 2021 to September 2024. 1,261 DUI convictions in 11 months of 2025. Neither figure counts breath tests.
cards.sub: The 149 covers Section 44 only (death or injury). The 1,261 spans Sections 44, 45 and 45A, January to November 2025.

cards.big: 12 fatal crashes caused by drunk road users in 2024, 0.19% of all fatal crashes. Testing is discretionary. The real number is unknown.
cards.sub: Police need 'reasonable cause' to demand a breath test. In New South Wales, police can arrest a driver in a fatal crash for blood and urine tests.

cards.big: 4,340 motorcyclists killed in 2025. 13.7% of accidents, 66.4% of deaths. The gig economy's youngest workers on the deadliest vehicles.
cards.sub: 73.98% of riders rely on it as main income. His widow is pursuing separate legal action. The MMA called for a victim compensation fund. None exists.

cards.big: Penalties already exist. The real question is whether Malaysia detects drunk drivers before they kill, and whether alcohol is even the main killer of motorcyclists.
Deterrence requires detection. Compensation requires architecture. 4,340 motorcyclists died in 2025: most sober, on roads not built for them, riding because they had no other way.
